$comment: Canonical catalog of the 20 Rosary mysteries plus the fixed illustration keys used by steps not tied to a specific mystery. imageKey doubles as the lookup key into MysteryTranslations (title/fruit/description per language) and the filename stem under Shared/Images/{imageKey}.jpg. Source of truth: Windows's Models/MysteryCatalog.cs (this file was built from it); iOS's Mocks/Content/MysteryCatalog.swift and Android's content/MysteryCatalog.kt must carry the exact same set/order. Keep in sync — see README.markdown in this directory. An alternate eastern-icon artwork set ships as Shared/Images/eastern_{imageKey}.jpg — the same 20 keys behind an eastern_ prefix, selected per favorite by RosaryOptions.mysteryImageStyle and resolved at build time into RosaryStep.imageVariantKey; a display variant only, never part of this catalog.

overrideImages.note: Not a classical painting like the rest — a small generated placeholder graphic, one per platform (see ARCHITECTURE.markdown#assets).

franciscanCrownSevenJoys.$comment: The Franciscan Crown's Seven Joys of Mary — a devotion-specific ordered list of imageKeys, not a MysteryGroup (adding a 5th case to MysteryGroup would pollute a type that's otherwise exclusively about the 4 traditional Rosary sets). The authoritative copy of this list is the inline decades.entries in Shared/content/franciscanCrown/devotion.json. Six of the seven reuse mysteries.mysteries entries above outright, resolving cross-bundle from the rosary pack's merged tables; only order 4 (Adoration of the Magi) is new content, shipped in the franciscanCrown bundle's own mysteries maps (all six languages) — deliberately the ONLY mystery that bundle ships, so it never overrides the Rosary's own content.

newImageKeys.note: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Adoration of the Magi (c. 1655-60), Toledo Museum of Art — public domain, shipped inside the bundle; see Shared/Images/CREDITS.markdown.
